title: Watchlist
html:
Nov 9, 2026: "my watchlist should not be stagnant. If you see we don't have enough plays, feel free to add and remove tickers that fit our themes." He also said Claude can ask him to chart a ticker as themes grow and change, so we can see how it develops.

This doc is the master list. The frontmatter tickers: line is the current list (it also drives the ticker buttons on Market Desk). His Webull list "2026 Grow" is kept in sync with it. A ticker that is not on the tickers: line never appears in any report (claude/desk-rules.md section 3b).

The value rule (the desk, Nov 18, 2026)

"If a ticker on our watch list doesn't provide us with value we need to remove or replace it. What provides value? Either has options that we can trade. Options that are within our budget and are liquid for us to enter and exit. Or having them on the list gives us signals for other tickers that we track." Every name on the list must be one of:

  • Tradable: a contract near the money with delta ≥ 0.20 for ≤ $800 that passes the liquidity rule (OI ≥ 500, about 50 a day, spread ≤ 10% of mid). Note if it is calls only or puts only.
  • Signal: it tells us something about other names we trade (SPY, QQQ, IWM, SMH, XLE, TLT, and names whose contracts cost over $800 near the money but lead their group: DELL, AMD, BE, TSLA, CRDO, VRT).

A name that is neither gets removed or replaced. Every Friday Weekly Coaching re-checks the list against this rule. Nov 21, 2026: "we need to ensure that we are looking at liquid options only. we do not want to get stuck in a trade." Liquidity is checked on the contract actually used, at the moment of entry, never assumed from an earlier screen.

The $40 floor (the desk, Nov 19, 2026)

"I do not like having stocks under $40 on the watchlist." No name priced under $40 goes on the list, and a name that closes a week (Friday) under $40 comes off in that Friday's Weekly Coaching. Applied to ETFs as well (DRAM came off at $38.43). Removed Nov 19 under this rule: SMCI ($23.84), NU ($11.82), DRAM ($38.43). Close to the line, to watch: OXY ($53.81) and INTC ($55.72) are above it.

Current list (31)

  • Core 7: SPY, AAPL, TSLA, XOM, NOW, DELL, PLTR
  • Travel: DAL, BA
  • AI & semis: NVDA, INTC, AMD, SMH, BE, ORCL, ANT, CRDO
  • AI power & data-center build-out: VRT
  • Mega-cap & others: AMZN, GOOGL, SPCX, KO, OXY
  • Banks: JPM, BAC
  • Retail trading & commerce: HOOD, SHOP
  • Gauges: QQQ, IWM, XLE, TLT (the S&P 500 index, SPX, is the main gauge in every report per voice.md; SPY stays only for its options)

Removed Nov 18 (the desk: "Remove."): HLT, RCL and CCL. Removed Nov 19 (the $40 floor): SMCI, NU, DRAM. Still flagged, his call: SHOP (14–23% spreads in December).

Added Nov 21, 2026 (the desk’s adds: JPM, BAC)

Nov 21: "yes add JPM and BAC to the list", after asking for "other liquid and profitable investment ideas" because the ideas lean too heavily on one trade (AI). A screen of 32 non-AI stocks and ETFs on Nov 21 found most of them failing on the contracts (PG $170 C 10.8% spread, JNJ $270 C 18% and $895, MRK $130 P 15%, UNH $320 P $963, COST over $4,000, XLP/XLF/XLI near-the-money Dec contracts with very wide closing quotes). Numbers are the Nov 20 close; contracts are Dec 18. Re-check before any play. Theme: banks (credit and rates, a driver outside AI).

  • JPM (JPMorgan Chase): $310.53 (−10.3% on the week). Sits on the 61.8% retracement of the Mar 12 low $275.06 → Aug 13 high $364.68 run ($309.30); 50% $319.87, 78.6% $294.24. Broke its 200-day ($322.88). The 14-day crossed under the 30-day on Nov 20 (direction down); the 50-day ($336.81) is still over the 200-day (trend up). RSI 31. Puts tradable: $300 P bid/ask $6.70/$7.35 (9% spread), OI 4,663, vol 2,458, delta −0.32, IV 35.3% vs 20-day moves 31% = RICH 1.14. The $310 P (spread 16.5%, OI 2,004) and $310 C (spread 18%, OI 995) fail the liquidity rule. Setup to watch: a bounce into the $320–323 cluster (the 50% retracement plus the broken 200-day) that fails back under $320, stop over $328, target the 78.6% $294.24 (about 3.2 to 1); at $320 the $300 P's delta falls near 0.22, so the strike has to be re-checked at the trigger.
  • BAC (Bank of America): $47.04 (−7.8% on the week). Direction down since Sep 2 and trend down (50-day $52.69 under the 200-day $54.38); 52-week low $45.64; RSI 28. Puts tradable at one strike: $47 P bid/ask $1.79/$1.95 (8.6% spread), OI 4,066, vol 1,207, delta −0.49, about $187, IV 34.6% vs 20-day moves 27% = EXPENSIVE 1.28. The $45 P (10.5% spread), the $47 C (OI 446) and the $50 C (16% spread) fail. Calls thin for now; $47 is $7 above the $40 floor.
  • Neither has a Fib drawing of the desk’s yet. Both are his own adds (protected).
  • Considered and not added: WMT. Its Dec 18 $130 C is liquid (bid/ask $3.00/$3.30, OI 8,903, vol 3,209), but the desk’s concern is the range: $102–135 since May, now near the top ($127.95 vs the May high $134.83 and the Nov high $131.82).

Added Nov 20, 2026 (the desk’s adds: CRDO, VRT)

Nov 20 (just after midnight): "add CRDO, VRT to the watchlist." Numbers are the Nov 19 close; contracts are Dec 18. Re-check before any play.

  • CRDO (Credo Technology; high-speed connectivity chips and cables for AI data centers): $117.76 (−4.2% on Nov 19; day range $117.21–$131.15). Far off its $308.67 52-week high, 36% above its $86.49 low: a broken AI-hardware leader. Options are very expensive and thin near the money: $120 C bid/ask $14.20/$15.20 (about $1,470, delta 0.52, OI 274, vol 59), $115 P $13.20/$14.30 (about $1,375, OI 1,345, vol 352), $110 P $10.90/$11.90 (about $1,140, OI 546), $130 C $8.50/$11.10 (about $980, 27% spread). IV about 116–119%. Nothing near the money under $800: signal only for now (it reads the AI-networking trade with NVDA, AMD, SMH). Check its next earnings date before any play; a report before Dec 18 would put earnings inside the expiry.
  • VRT (Vertiv; power and cooling for AI data centers): $184.99 (−4.9% on Nov 19; day range $183.81–$201.42). About half its $379.76 52-week high, 25% above its $147.72 low. Options near the money cost $1,000–1,600: $185 C $14.85/$16.75 (about $1,580, delta 0.51, OI 321, vol 16), $185 P $14.25/$15.50 (OI 1,283, vol 248), $195 C $10.40/$11.55 (about $1,100, OI 419), $175 P $9.95/$11.00 (about $1,050, OI 1,164). IV about 69–73%. Signal only for now (AI power demand; reads with BE, DELL and the AI-capex theme). Under the $800 cap would need strikes further out or a shorter expiry; re-check after the volatility settles.
  • Neither has a Fib drawing of the desk’s yet. Both are his own adds (protected).

Added Nov 19, 2026 (the desk’s add: ANT)

Nov 19: "we are going to be adding ANT to the watchlist."

  • ANT (Anthropic; AI): first day of trading Nov 19, 2026. Priced at $83, opened $111.50, high $115.10, low $92.72, closed $97.17 (+17.1% from the $83 price), volume about 857 million shares. Amazon and Alphabet own stakes, so it moves the AI-backer trade (AMZN −3.9% and GOOGL −3.5% on the debut day).
  • Options: none listed yet (Webull showed no ANT contracts on the night of Nov 19). New listings usually get options a few days after the debut. Watch only, no plays, until contracts list and pass the liquidity rule and the $800 cap. No Fib drawing of the desk’s yet; a fresh IPO has no swing history, so levels start from the debut day's range ($92.72–115.10) and the $83 offer price.

Option screen, Nov 18, 2026 (Dec 18 contracts, live morning quotes)

  • Tradable both ways: PLTR, INTC, HOOD, ORCL, GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN, NVDA, KO, XOM, BA, SPCX, NOW, IWM, TLT, XLE.
  • Calls only (puts too thin): OXY, DAL. (Nov 20: the DAL $80 P passed for one session, $4.05/$4.40, OI 2,853, vol 6,129; DAL becomes tradable both ways only if the puts keep passing.)
  • Puts only (calls thin), from Nov 21: JPM, BAC.
  • Signal only (near-the-money Dec contracts over $800): SMH, DELL, AMD, BE, TSLA, QQQ (and, from Nov 20, CRDO and VRT); SPY's Dec calls at the money cost about $1,500–1,900 (use shorter expirations or strikes further out).
  • Removed for no value: V (puts 12–20% spreads, 13–18 traded a strike, OI under 2,000; the desk: "I wanted to short visa but there's literally no volume in any of the contracts"), ABNB (1–9 traded a strike, 20–23% spreads), RTX (1–15 traded a strike).

Rules for changing it

  1. When.
    • Changes are made only in the Friday Weekly Coaching or the Sunday Week Ahead.
    • At most 3 adds and 3 removes a week.
    • Mon–Thu reports may flag a candidate in one line ("on deck for the watchlist") but don't change the list.
    • the desk’s own adds and removes go in whenever he asks and don't count against the quota.
  2. Add a name only if all of these hold:
    • it is priced at $40 or more;
    • it fits a theme in claude/themes.md (or a new theme with real evidence: earnings, news, money flow);
    • it has a clear setup on the chart (trend plus a Fib level, a breakout, a breakdown);
    • its options pass the liquidity rule (OI ≥ 500, ~50 contracts a day, spread ≤ 10% of mid);
    • it has a contract near the money with delta ≥ 0.20 for ≤ $800, or will once it pulls back. Prefer names that fill a gap: too few plays, all plays on one side (all calls or all puts), or a theme with no tradable name.
  3. Remove a name only if:
    • it fails the value rule above; or
    • it closes a week under $40; or
    • it has produced no play and no top-name ladder for 4+ weeks; or
    • its options have gone thin; or
    • its theme has faded.
  4. Never remove without the desk saying so:
    • the core 7 and the gauges;
    • any name with a WATCHING idea on the scorecard;
    • any name with his own levels in fib-style.md;
    • any name in his current ideas (claude/themes.md);
    • any name he added himself (HOOD, SHOP, INTC, ANT, CRDO, VRT, JPM, BAC).
  5. Each change:
    • Update the Webull list "2026 Grow" with add_watchlist_instruments / remove_watchlist_instruments. Those are watchlist edits only, never orders.
    • Update this doc: the tickers: line, the current list, and a log line.
    • In the report, add a short "Watchlist changes" section: what was added or removed, the theme, and one line of why.
    • If the Webull edit fails, say so in the final message and keep this doc as the master list.
  6. A removed name leaves every report at once (Nov 19, 2026; claude/desk-rules.md section 3b). Any paper play still open on it closes at the next mark, noted "closed: name removed from the watchlist".

Chart requests (ask the desk to draw his ladder)

  • When to ask:
    • a name is added and becomes a top idea;
    • a theme's leader has none of his levels;
    • one of his drawings looks outdated (a new major swing has formed).
  • How: through the single Sunday ask, "Your chart and call this week" (see growth-log.md). It names the ticker and the move to swing, e.g. "the Oct low → Nov high run".
    • He sends the thinkorswim Drawing Properties screen (begin/middle/end values and dates), like his Nov 9 XOM, V and BE screens, plus his call.
    • One name a week (two at most), and at most 2 open requests at a time.
  • When he sends one:
    • Add it to fib-style.md under "His levels" with the date drawn.
    • Grade it forward only, from that date.
  • Open requests:
    • INTC extension on the Jun 30 high $142.35 → Nov 5 low $51.51 drop, plus his call (asked in the Nov 22 Week Ahead).
    • SPY extension on the Mar 30 low $626.11 → Oct 6 record high $781.62 run, plus his call (asked in the Nov 15 Week Ahead). Since Nov 19 the gauge is SPX; the same run on SPX works.
  • Filled:
    • AMZN extension anchors (asked Nov 9; sent Nov 14, now in fib-style.md).

Added Nov 15, 2026, late (the desk’s adds: HOOD, SHOP)

Nov 15: "Let's add HOOD, SHOP." Numbers are the Nov 13 close; contracts are Dec 18. Re-check before any play.

  • HOOD (Robinhood; retail trading and crypto activity): $77.86. Down about 38% from the September high near $125 with lower highs every month since; now back into its spring 2026 base ($66–77). Downtrend. Puts are liquid: $75 P $470 mid (bid/ask $4.60/$4.75, OI 9,755, vol 1,599), $80 P $720 mid (bid/ask $7.05/$7.35, OI 13,948). The $80 call fails the spread rule tonight (bid/ask $5.00/$5.75, 14%). IV about 64%.
  • SHOP (Shopify; online commerce): $147.09. Off its $180.88 October high but still in the uptrend that started from about $94 in May; the summer base is $144–155. Options are borderline: $150 C $760 mid (bid/ask $7.15/$8.05, 12% spread, OI 3,474, vol 614); the $145 put's spread is 26%. Watch only until spreads tighten under 10%.
  • Neither has a Fib drawing of the desk’s yet.

Added Nov 15, 2026 (the desk’s swap: INTC in for MU)

Nov 15: "I don't think realistically I will be trading MU's option contracts. Can we replace MU with INTC?" Numbers are the Nov 13 close; contracts are Dec 18. Re-check before any play.

  • INTC (AI & semis): $59.66. Ran from about $33 (Nov 2025) to a $142.35 high (Jun 30, 2026), then fell; it gapped from $92.07 to $65.76 on Oct 30 and made a $51.51 low on Nov 5. Downtrend: under its 50-day (about $92) and 200-day (about $88, from weekly closes; recompute from daily bars). It sits just under the 78.6% retracement of the Mar 30 low $40.63 → Jun 30 high run ($62.40), with the 78.6% of the full Nov 2025 → Jun 2026 run at about $56.31 below. Options are liquid and cheap enough on both sides: $60 C $477.50 mid (bid/ask $4.70/$4.85, OI 24,301, vol 1,089, delta 0.52), $60 P $487.50 mid (bid/ask $4.80/$4.95, OI 20,861, vol 1,351), IV about 65%. No earnings inside Dec 18 expected (verify). No Fib drawing of the desk’s yet.
  • MU removed at the desk’s request (on Nov 8 its only Dec contract under $800 was the $950 call with a 0.12 delta).

Added Nov 11, 2026 (the desk approved adding them ahead of the Friday review)

Screened from 10 names. Numbers are the Nov 11 close; contracts are Dec 18. Re-check before any play.

  • OXY (oil shock): on the tested edge. Price $57.24 and its 50-day $59.82 are above the 200-day $56.29, RSI 39.6. $57.50 C ~$214 (bid/ask $2.06/$2.21, OI 3,369, vol 1,255), IV 31% vs moves 32% → FAIR. Reported Nov 9.
  • CCL (travel, cruise): removed Nov 18.
  • RTX (defense): removed Nov 18 (thin options).
  • ORCL (AI infrastructure capex, put side): downtrend under both averages, $128.38 after an 8.8% bounce; 52-week low $109.21. Fills the put gap. $120 P ~$720 (bid/ask $7.10/$7.30, OI 20,452, vol 2,644), IV 70% vs moves 62% → FAIR, but earnings Dec 14 fall inside the Dec 18 expiry. Setup: a failed rally into the 50-day (~$137).
  • Passed over: UAL (the $120 C spread is 14%, the $115 C costs $878), CRWD (at-the-money call ~$2,000, OI 471), AVGO (put ~$2,000), WMT (earnings around Nov 19 inside the expiry), BAC and UBER (no clear setup).

Log (newest first)

  • 2026-11-22 | Week Ahead review: no adds or removes (the list changed Nov 21 with the desk’s JPM and BAC; no name meets a remove rule; every name is over $40, INTC closest at $51.28). New open chart request: INTC extension on the Jun 30 → Nov 5 drop plus his call (2 open requests with the SPX ask, the maximum). Webull "2026 Grow" unchanged.
  • 2026-11-21 | the desk’s adds (in chat): JPM and BAC, in a new "Banks" group, to cut the list's reliance on the AI trade. Both over $40; puts liquid at one or more near-the-money Dec strikes, calls thin. WMT considered and not added (range $102–135 since May, price near the top). Webull "2026 Grow" synced (both added). List now 31. His own adds, outside the weekly quota.
  • 2026-11-20 | the desk’s adds (in chat): CRDO and VRT. Both over $40; near-the-money Dec contracts cost over $800 with thin volume and high IV, so both start as signal names. Webull "2026 Grow" synced (both added). List now 29. His own adds, outside the weekly quota.
  • 2026-11-19 | the desk’s changes (in chat): added ANT (Anthropic, first trading day; watch only until options list) and set a $40 floor ("I do not like having stocks under $40 on the watchlist"). Removed under it: SMCI ($23.84), NU ($11.82) and DRAM ($38.43, an ETF; removed under the same floor). Webull "2026 Grow" synced (ANT added; SMCI, NU, DRAM removed). List now 27. Rule 6 replaced: removed names leave every report at once. His own changes, outside the weekly quota.
  • 2026-11-18 | the desk: "Remove." HLT, RCL and CCL taken off the master list to match Webull "2026 Grow", which already lacked them. List and Webull now match at 29. Travel is now DAL and BA.
  • 2026-11-18 | the desk’s changes (in chat, after a live option screen of every name): removed V, ABNB and RTX for options with no real volume; added NU (in place of ABNB; MELI was over budget). Value rule added. Webull "2026 Grow" synced (V, ABNB, RTX removed; NU added). His own changes, outside the weekly quota.

  • 2026-11-15 | the desk’s swap (in chat, after the Week Ahead): removed MU (he won't realistically trade its options), added INTC. Webull "2026 Grow" synced (MU removed, INTC added). List stays at 32. This change is the desk’s own, outside the weekly add/remove quota.

AMZN chart request marked filled (sent Nov 14); new open request: SPY extension plus his call. Webull "2026 Grow" unchanged.

No adds (the Nov 11 adds used the week's quota). List now 32. Webull "2026 Grow" synced (LMT, OSCR, ET removed).
  • 2026-11-11 | Added OXY, CCL, RTX, ORCL (the desk’s OK, ahead of the Friday review; these count as this week's 3-add limit plus one). Synced Webull "2026 Grow": it was missing TLT, now added; Webull and this list now match at 35.
